title: Forces and their interactions; Work done and energy transfer

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Weight
items.clue: The force acting on an object due to gravity.

items.label: Newtonmeter
items.clue: A calibrated spring-balance used to measure forces.

items.label: Mass
items.clue: The quantity of matter in an object, measured in kilograms.

items.label: Directly proportional
items.clue: One quantity is a fixed multiple of another: double one and the other doubles.

questions.stem: Which statement about the weight of a book resting on a shelf is correct?

options.text: It is the total amount of matter contained in the book.
It is the push of the shelf upwards on the book.
It is a property the book has whatever happens.
It is the force acting on the book due to gravity.

questions.explanation: Weight is the force acting on an object due to gravity, which close to the Earth is due to its gravitational field.

questions.stem: What is meant by the resultant force on an object?

options.text: The largest of all of the forces that are acting on the object.
The force that is left once the object has stopped moving.
The single force with the same effect as all of them together.
The total of the sizes of every force that acts on it.

questions.explanation: A number of forces may be replaced by a single force with the same effect: the resultant force.

questions.stem: In which of these situations is work done on the object by the force described?

options.text: A sledge is dragged forwards and slides 5 m over snow
A cleaner pushes hard on a crate that does not move
A waiter carries a tray level across a room
A student holds a bag of books still for a minute

questions.explanation: The pulling force causes a displacement of the sledge along its own line of action, so work is done on the sledge.

questions.stem: An astronaut takes a 3 kg toolbox from the Earth (g = 9.8 N/kg) to the Moon (g = 1.6 N/kg). What happens?

options.text: Its mass and weight both fall, because gravity is weaker there.
Its mass and weight both drop to about a sixth.
Its mass stays at 3 kg but its weight becomes smaller.
Its mass and its weight do not change on the way there.

questions.explanation: Mass does not depend on location; weight depends on the gravitational field strength at that point.

questions.stem: A box is pulled to the right with a force of 12 N while a friction force of 5 N acts to the left. What is the resultant force?

options.text: 17 N, acting to the right
12 N acting to the right
7 N acting to the left
7 N acting to the right

questions.explanation: For forces in a straight line the resultant is 12 - 5 = 7 N, in the direction of the larger force.

questions.stem: A student holds a box of weight 40 N still at chest height for 15 s. How much work does the student's upward force do on the box?

options.text: 0 J

questions.explanation: The box has no displacement, so s = 0 and W = 40 × 0 = 0 J.

questions.stem: Which equation is used to calculate the weight of an object?

options.text: weight = mass ÷ the gravitational field strength
weight = mass plus gravitational field strength
mass = weight × gravitational field strength g
weight = mass × gravitational field strength

questions.explanation: This is the equation exactly as the specification gives it, W = m g.

questions.stem: In the equation work done = force × distance, what is meant by the distance?

options.text: The total length of the path that the object takes
The distance the object moves, in any direction
The distance moved along the line of action of the force
The time for which the force carries on acting

questions.explanation: The specification defines the distance as the distance moved along the line of action of the force.

questions.stem: A rock has a mass of 12 kg. The gravitational field strength is 9.8 N/kg. What is the weight of the rock?
questions.explanation: W = m g = 12 × 9.8 = 117.6 N, with weight in newtons.

questions.stem: A force of 25 N pushes a trolley 8 m along the line of action of the force. How much work is done on the trolley?

options.text: 3.125 joules
0.32 joules
33 joules
200 joules

questions.explanation: W = F s = 25 × 8 = 200 J, with the distance measured along the line of action of the force.

questions.stem: A bag has a weight of 49 N at a place where the gravitational field strength is 9.8 N/kg. What is the mass of the bag?

options.text: 5 kg
0.2 kg

questions.explanation: Rearranging W = m g gives m = W ÷ g = 49 ÷ 9.8 = 5 kg.

questions.stem: A crane does 3000 J of work on a load using a force of 250 N. How far does the load move along the line of action of the force?
questions.explanation: Rearranging W = F s gives s = W ÷ F = 3000 ÷ 250 = 12 m.

questions.stem: A ball hangs at rest on the end of a string. A free body diagram of the ball is drawn. Which forces should appear on it?

options.text: The tension in the string and the pull of the ball on the string as well.
The weight of the ball and the pull of the ball on the Earth below.
The weight of the ball and the tension in the string, both acting on the ball.
No forces at all, because the ball is hanging still on the string.

questions.explanation: A free body diagram shows the isolated object with only the forces that act on it.

questions.stem: A parachutist falls at a steady speed. Her weight is 700 N. What can be said about the forces on her?

options.text: The forces cancel out, so really no force acts at all.
Air resistance is 700 N upwards, so the resultant force is zero.
Her weight and the air resistance are an action pair.
No forces act on her now, since her speed is not changing.

questions.explanation: The forces are balanced: an upward 700 N air resistance and a 700 N weight give a resultant of zero.

questions.stem: A single force is resolved into two components acting at right angles to each other. Which statement is correct?

options.text: The two components together have the same effect as the force.
The two components add up numerically to the size of the single force.
Each component is exactly half the size of the original single force.
The two components replace a force that has no direction.

questions.explanation: The two component forces together have the same effect as the single force they replace.

questions.stem: Two forces at right angles act on a point. A student draws them to scale, head to tail, to find the resultant. What must the final answer state?

options.text: The magnitude in newtons only, since that is the number asked for.
The magnitude in newtons and the direction of the force.
The direction only, because a scale drawing cannot give a size.
The magnitude in newtons and the total length of both arrows.

questions.explanation: The resultant is a vector, so the answer gives both magnitude and direction from the scale drawing.
